author: marketing_c
protectedRevelations: Constitution of limits, future-scenario verdicts and institutional recommendations

scenes.title: Everyone followed procedure
scenes.viewerPurpose: See a patient hurt despite everyone following rules Look for harm without one obvious culprit
scenes.composition: A treatment appeal passes between ordinary desks while its patient waits
addOrChange: Add the patient and avoid devil imagery.

cues.narration: A patient loses treatment, yet everyone involved can explain why they followed the rules.
cues.visualAction: Each worker displays a completed form while treatment remains unavailable.

cues.narration: The Thousand-Handed Devil investigates harm that has no single pair of hands.
cues.visualAction: Follow the same appeal through the ordinary chain of hands.

scenes.title: The person between offices
scenes.viewerPurpose: Recognize the problem across public and private systems Picture protective rules becoming a maze
scenes.composition: The case spans a clinical desk and automated decision
addOrChange: Replace literal maze imagery with a missing handoff between records.

cues.narration: Its subject is modern responsibility, from public services to companies and automated decisions.
cues.visualAction: Show the case at both clinical and automated desks.

cues.narration: Rules meant to protect people can become a maze that nobody sees from end to end.
cues.visualAction: Each desk sees its own part while the patient faces the whole problem.

scenes.title: Where responsibility goes
scenes.viewerPurpose: Keep the suffering person in view Notice the appeal of being offered one simple enemy
scenes.composition: The patient seeks someone able to alter the decision
addOrChange: Add a simplistic public blame message separately from the actual causal chain.

cues.narration: The person suffering still needs someone who can understand the problem and change it.
cues.visualAction: Bring the appeal to a person with possible decision authority.

cues.narration: The book connects that frustration with the appeal of leaders promising one simple enemy.
cues.visualAction: Show the easy blame message while the actual problem remains unsolved.

scenes.title: Beyond the convenient villain
scenes.viewerPurpose: Follow decisions rather than settling for a villain Ask where responsibility could actually change the outcome
scenes.composition: A reviewer follows the actual decisions back through their records
addOrChange: Keep the patient visible and avoid assigning all harm to one villain.

cues.narration: It asks you to look past the easy villain and follow the decisions that allowed the harm.
cues.visualAction: Open the consequential decisions in their original order.

cues.narration: Where should responsibility live when power is spread across a thousand ordinary actions?
cues.visualAction: Hold patient and decision-makers together with responsibility still under examination.
